questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A point on a bow string is in equilibrium. The archer pulls horizontally with 160 N. Two equal string tensions act symmetrically, each at 75° to the horizontal. Calculate the tension in the string.
markPoints: Resolve the two tension forces in the horizontal direction and equate their resultant to 160 N.
Obtain T ≈ 310 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A gamma photon has wavelength 1.25 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Calculate the energy of one photon.
markPoints: Use E = hc/λ (or an equivalent two-step route using f).
Obtain 1.59 × 10⁻¹¹ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A transparent layer is 89 nm thick and light in the layer has wavelength 356 nm. Light reflects from the upper and lower surfaces; any equal reflection phase changes can be ignored. Explain why destructive interference occurs.
markPoints: The two reflected waves are in antiphase (180° or π rad apart).
The lower reflection travels an extra 2 × 89 nm = 178 nm.
178 nm is half of 356 nm, so the path difference is λ/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Sunlight reflected from a lake surface is horizontally polarised, while light reflected from submerged objects is unpolarised. Explain why Polaroid sunglasses can make the submerged objects easier to see. Include the nature of unpolarised light, what polarisation means, and the relative effect of the sunglasses on the two reflected beams.
markPoints: Unpolarised transverse light has oscillations in more than one plane perpendicular to energy transfer.
Polarisation restricts transverse oscillations to one plane.
With the transmission axis chosen appropriately, the horizontally polarised glare is greatly reduced.
The unpolarised light from submerged objects is only partly reduced, so contrast improves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A free neutron decays. Identify which fundamental interaction is responsible and explain why.
markPoints: Weak nuclear interaction.
The decay involves leptons and/or a change of quark flavour (for example d → u).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A 0.200 g indigestion tablet contains Mg(OH)₂. Add 40.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ HCl in excess. Mg(OH)₂ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + 2H₂O. The leftover acid needs 29.25 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. Calculate the percentage by mass of Mg(OH)₂.
markPoints: Initial HCl = 0.00800 mol.
NaOH, hence leftover HCl, = 0.002925 mol.
HCl reacting with Mg(OH)₂ = 0.005075 mol.
Mass Mg(OH)₂ ≈ 0.148 g.
Percentage ≈ 74.0%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A student makes a sodium carbonate standard solution by weighing about 2.5 g, dissolving it in a beaker, pouring into a 250 cm³ volumetric flask, then filling until the top of the meniscus reaches the line. Suggest three improvements.
markPoints: Record masses accurately / use weighing by difference or quantitative transfer.
Transfer all washings from beaker/stirring rod/container to the volumetric flask.
Use a dropper near the mark and set the bottom of the meniscus on the line.
Stopper and invert several times to mix thoroughly. Any three valid points score.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A Group 2 nitrate M(NO₃)₂ decomposes: 2M(NO₃)₂ → 2MO + 4NO₂ + O₂. A 0.320 g sample gives 225 cm³ of gas at 450 °C and 101000 Pa. Using R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, determine Mr of M(NO₃)₂ and identify M.
questions.modelAnswer: Convert V = 225 × 10⁻⁶ m³ and T = 723 K. pV = nRT gives 3.78 × 10⁻³ mol gas. 2 mol nitrate give 5 mol gas, so nitrate = 1.51 × 10⁻³ mol. Mr ≈ 211.9. Ar(M) ≈ 87.9, so M is Sr.
markPoints: Correct SI unit conversions.
Find total gas moles using pV=nRT.
Use 2:5 nitrate:gas ratio.
Identify strontium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For A(aq) + 2B(aq) ⇌ C(aq), ΔH = −32 kJ mol⁻¹. The temperature is decreased. Predict the effect on Kc and explain.
markPoints: Kc increases.
Lower temperature favours the exothermic direction.
The equilibrium shifts to release heat / oppose the temperature decrease.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Given 5cos²y − 4sin²y = 0: (a) find the exact possible values of tan y; (b) solve for all y in 0° ≤ y ≤ 360°, to the nearest 0.1°.
markPoints: Use an identity to reduce to one trig function.
Obtain tan²y = 5/4.
Obtain tan y = ±√5/2 exactly.
Find at least two correct angles from the tangent values.
Give all four correct solutions and no extras.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 5(b)
questions.prompt: The line 6x − 2y + 5 = 0 is tangent to y = x√x + k. Find k.
markPoints: Rearrange the line to obtain gradient 3.
Differentiate x√x = x^(3/2).
Set derivative equal to 3 to find the contact x-value.
Use the contact point on the tangent.
Obtain k = 6.5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: For C₁: y = 2x² − 20x + 42: (a) write it as a(x−b)²+c; (b) state its minimum point; (c) C₁ is stretched vertically so the new minimum is (5,−4). Find the new curve equation.
questions.modelAnswer: C₁: y = 2(x−5)² − 8. Minimum (5,−8). Vertical scale factor 1/2, so C₂: y = (x−5)² − 4.
markPoints: Minimum point (5,−8).
Use vertical stretch scale factor 1/2.
Obtain y=(x−5)²−4.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 8(b)
questions.prompt: For y = 6 − 12/√x, regions on either side of the x-axis between x=1 and x=a have equal area. Find a and fully justify it.
markPoints: Recognise equal positive/negative areas imply the signed integral from 1 to a is zero.
Use the integral result 6a − 24√a + 18 = 0.
Solve the resulting equation.
Conclude a = 9 with a valid justification.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 10(b)
questions.prompt: A car is worth £18,000 at t=0 and £12,000 after 2 years. Its value is modelled by V = Ae^(−kt). Find t when V = £10,000, to 2 significant figures.
markPoints: Find k≈0.203.
Obtain t≈2.9 years.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: In brachytherapy a sealed source is placed beside a small tumour. Explain one advantage of using beta radiation rather than gamma radiation.
markPoints: Beta is more ionising and/or less penetrating than gamma.
Link the lower penetration or greater ionisation to a more localised tumour dose / less damage to neighbouring healthy tissue.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A screen is viewed from 0.50 m. Two dark pixels separated by one light pixel should just fail to be resolved. Take cone diameter at the fovea as 1.5 μm and eye length as 21 mm. Determine the minimum pixel line density in pixels per cm.
markPoints: Use similar triangles / a consistent angular-resolution ratio.
Relate retinal separation to about two cone diameters.
Obtain about 140 pixels per cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Define sound intensity.
markPoints: Sound power per unit area, or equivalently energy transferred per unit area per second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A sound has intensity level L dB. By how many decibels does the level increase if the sound intensity doubles?
markPoints: Doubling intensity raises sound intensity level by approximately 3 dB.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An ultrasound scan produces a two-dimensional image of a kidney rather than a single amplitude-versus-time trace. Identify the scan type.
markPoints: B-scan / brightness scan, because it forms an image.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An ECG pad uses a sticky backing gel. Explain one additional reason the gel is needed, give one suitable extra property of the gel, and state one way the skin should be prepared before applying the pad.
markPoints: The gel improves electrical contact.
A suitable property is low electrical resistance, non-irritating, or chemically unreactive with skin products.
Prepare the skin by removing hair / shaving, gently abrading, cleaning or drying it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The stomach is poorly visible on an ordinary X-ray image. Explain a method used to improve its visibility.
markPoints: The patient ingests a barium meal / suitable X-ray contrast medium.
Barium strongly absorbs/attenuates X-rays, increasing image contrast in the stomach.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A negatively charged metal plate discharges under electromagnetic radiation. Explain how the photoelectric effect causes the discharge, why there is a threshold frequency, and why increasing intensity above threshold increases the rate of discharge.
markPoints: Photoelectrons leave the surface and carry away negative charge.
A single photon must provide at least the work function.
Photon energy is hf, so a minimum energy gives a threshold frequency.
At fixed frequency above threshold, greater intensity means more photons per second.
More photons per second can release more electrons per second, so discharge is faster.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Photoelectrons have maximum kinetic energy 1.1 eV when the incident frequency is 1.2 × 10^15 Hz. Calculate the metal's work function in eV.
markPoints: Use photon energy E=hf.
Use hf = work function + maximum kinetic energy.
Obtain about 3.9 eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Electrons are sent faster at a graphite target and the diffraction rings become smaller. Explain why.
markPoints: Greater electron speed gives greater momentum.
de Broglie wavelength decreases because λ=h/p.
A shorter wavelength relative to the graphite spacing produces less diffraction, so the ring diameter decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A uniform 1800 N platform is suspended by vertical cables 3.6 m apart. A 750 N worker stands distance d from the left end. When the left-cable tension is 1150 N, calculate d.
markPoints: Apply the principle of moments about a suitable point.
Include the platform weight at its centre and the worker weight at distance d.
Obtain d=2.4 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A cyclist and bicycle have total mass 65 kg on a slope of angle θ. Write an expression for the component of their weight parallel to the slope.
markPoints: Parallel component is mg sin θ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The same cyclist produces 310 W while moving steadily at 1.63 m s^-1 up the slope. Neglect air resistance. Calculate θ.
markPoints: Use P=Fv to find the force parallel to the slope.
Set this equal to mg sin θ and obtain θ≈17.4°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Explain in terms of electron motion why a filament lamp's resistance rises as voltage and current increase.
markPoints: Increasing voltage increases current / electron flow rate.
The filament becomes hotter and lattice-ion vibrations increase.
More electron-lattice collisions occur, increasing resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A 6.0 Ω lamp is connected in parallel with a 25 Ω variable-resistor section. Calculate the total resistance.
markPoints: Use the parallel-resistance relation.
Obtain about 4.84 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Using the circuit in the previous part with a 12 V battery and total resistance about 4.84 Ω, calculate the power transferred by the battery.
markPoints: Use P=V²/R or an equivalent power relation.
Obtain about 30 W.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Explain why first ionisation energy decreases down Group 2.
markPoints: The outer electron is in a higher shell / atoms are larger / shielding increases.
Attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron is weaker.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: 0.834 g of citric acid (Mr 192.0) is made up to 500 cm³. Calculate the concentration in mol dm^-3.
markPoints: Find moles using mass/Mr.
Convert 500 cm³ to 0.500 dm³.
Calculate c=n/V to obtain 0.00869 mol dm^-3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A titration method includes rinsing the burette only with distilled water, measuring the 25 cm³ aliquot with a measuring cylinder, and adding 5 cm³ of indicator. Identify three sources of inaccuracy, explain each, and state how to correct them.
markPoints: Rinse the burette with the titrant after distilled water so the titrant is not diluted.
Use a volumetric pipette, not a measuring cylinder, for the 25.0 cm³ aliquot.
Use only a few drops of indicator because a large volume changes the reacting mixture.
A strong answer links each error to why it affects the result and gives the correction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The C-Br bond is polar, but CBr4 is non-polar. Explain why.
markPoints: CBr4 is tetrahedral / symmetrical.
The bond dipoles cancel, so there is no overall permanent dipole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A 121Sb+ ion crosses a 1.05 m flight tube in 5.93×10^-4 s. All ions have the same kinetic energy. Calculate the mass of one 121Sb+ ion, then the flight time for 123Sb+.
markPoints: Use 121/(1000×NA) for the mass of one 121Sb+ ion.
Find speed from distance/time.
Use KE=1/2 mv².
Use equal kinetic energy or t² proportional to mass.
Obtain about 5.98×10^-4 s for 123Sb+.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: In acidic solution, iodate(V) oxidises iodide to iodine. Write the oxidation half-equation for iodide and the corresponding reduction half-equation for iodate(V).
markPoints: Correct iodide oxidation half-equation.
Correct iodate(V) reduction half-equation in acidic solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: For 3H2 + N2 ⇌ 2NH3 at 745 K, Kc=0.118 mol^-2 dm^6. A 0.150 dm³ equilibrium mixture contains 0.0285 mol H2 and 0.0870 mol N2. Calculate the amount of NH3.
markPoints: Write the correct Kc expression.
Convert H2 and N2 moles to concentrations.
Rearrange to obtain [NH3]².
Take the positive square root.
Multiply [NH3] by 0.150 dm³ to obtain about 3.25×10^-3 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Describe tests that show a colourless solution contains ammonium sulfate.
markPoints: Warm with aqueous NaOH.
Ammonia turns damp red litmus blue.
Add acidified barium chloride or barium nitrate to a fresh sample.
A white barium sulfate precipitate forms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: 5.0 g of a molybdenum oxide contains 4.0 g molybdenum. Ar(Mo)=95.9, Ar(O)=16.0. Determine the empirical formula.
markPoints: Correct option/formula: Mo2O3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Solve cos²y = 10 sin y + 4 for 0°<y<360°, giving answers to the nearest degree and justifying all solutions.
markPoints: Use cos²y=1−sin²y.
Form and solve a quadratic in sin y.
Reject the inadmissible sine value.
Find one correct angle for the valid sine value.
Give both 198° and 342°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Express 3x³+5x²−27x+10 in the form (x−2)(ax²+bx+c), with integers a,b,c.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 6(b)
questions.prompt: A and B are endpoints of a diameter, A(1,4), B(7,−2). Show that the circle can be written x²+y²−8x−2y=1.
markPoints: Find centre (4,1).
Find radius²=18.
Expand/rearrange to the required equation.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 6(c)
questions.prompt: The same circle crosses the x-axis at D and E and has centre C. Find the exact area of triangle DEC.
markPoints: Set y=0 and solve for the x-intercepts, or use Pythagoras from the centre.
Obtain half-base distance √17 or base 2√17.
Use the perpendicular height from C to the x-axis.
Obtain area √17.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: The curve y=a²−x² (a>0) encloses area 36 with the x-axis. Find a and justify fully.
markPoints: Find x-intercepts at ±a.
Integrate a²−x².
Use the limits −a to a (or symmetry).
Set the area expression equal to 36.
Solve 4a³/3=36.
Obtain a=3 with justification.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 8(c)
questions.prompt: For the curve in Question 8, the stationary x-values are ±√3. Find the coordinates and classify both stationary points, justifying your answer.
markPoints: Use the second derivative or derivative sign changes.
At x=√3 the second derivative is positive, giving a minimum.
At x=−√3 it is negative, giving a maximum.
Give both exact coordinates with correct classifications.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Let m and n be odd integers. Prove that m²+n² is divisible by 2 but not by 4.
markPoints: Represent the two odd integers correctly, e.g. 2p+1 and 2q+1.
Expand m²+n².
Factor out 2 to prove divisibility by 2.
Show the remaining factor is odd.
Conclude the expression is not divisible by 4.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: 10(a)
questions.prompt: For the curve y=√2/x² at the point with x=2, find the equation of the tangent.
markPoints: Rewrite using a negative power if useful.
Differentiate correctly.
Evaluate the gradient at x=2.
Use point-gradient form to obtain the tangent equation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An electron neutrino interacts with a chlorine-37 nucleus to form argon-37 and an electron. Explain, using conservation laws, why the electron must be emitted.
markPoints: Identify charge conservation or lepton-number conservation as relevant.
Show how the emitted electron allows both charge and lepton number to be conserved across the interaction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Calculate the specific charge of an argon-37 nucleus, using 18 protons and 37 nucleons.
markPoints: Use specific charge = charge / mass with charge 18e and mass approximately 37u.
Obtain about 4.6–4.7 × 10^7 C kg^-1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: In electron capture by argon-37, deduce the exchange particle and the change to the affected baryon, giving reasons.
markPoints: Identify W+ as the exchange particle.
State that a proton changes to a neutron / the baryon's charge decreases by one elementary charge.
Recognise this as a weak interaction / electron capture.
Support with a correct quark-flavour change such as u to d, or another valid conservation argument.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Explain the attractive and repulsive forces acting between nucleons, the exchange particles associated with them, and how the balance of these forces helps keep a nucleus stable.
markPoints: Electromagnetic repulsion acts between protons; gravitational attraction is negligible at nuclear scale.
The strong interaction can be attractive and very-short-range repulsive and acts between nucleons.
Pions are exchange particles associated with the strong interaction; virtual photons are associated with electromagnetic interaction.
The strong interaction dominates at normal nucleon separations and has only a short range.
Very-short-range strong repulsion helps stop nucleons collapsing into each other.
A high-quality answer links the ranges and relative strengths of the interactions to nuclear stability.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: An electron gains 6.7 eV of kinetic energy by moving through a potential difference V. Deduce V.
markPoints: For one electron, an energy gain of 6.7 eV corresponds to a potential difference of 6.7 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A mercury atom emits an ultraviolet photon of energy 6.7 eV. Calculate the wavelength of the photon.
markPoints: Convert 6.7 eV to joules.
Use E = hc/λ, or E=hf together with c=fλ.
Obtain approximately 1.9 × 10^-7 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A guitar string fixed at both ends is 0.648 m long and has a first-harmonic frequency of 147 Hz. Calculate the wave speed on the string.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: The same 0.648 m guitar string has tension 71 N and first-harmonic frequency 147 Hz. Calculate the mass of the vibrating length of string.
markPoints: Use the stationary-wave/string relation to find mass per unit length, or use v=sqrt(T/μ).
Use mass = μL.
Obtain approximately 1.3 × 10^-3 kg.
